A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Plan2Align, with identifiable continuity in the method, translation experiments, prompts, and appendix analyses. All pages, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original translation experiments, timing measurements, iteration and prompt ablations, and an alignment sanity check.

after.justification: V2 reports original translation and HH-RLHF experiments, GPT-4 comparisons, inference timings, and additional MetricX error analyses.

M1.justification: The buffer-and-rewrite framework remains, but v2 adds a response-generation adaptation using positional segments, propagated whole-response rewards, and sampling from top-k segments per position. Algorithm 1 also changes final output selection: v1 returns the last buffer-based rewrite, whereas v2 selects the highest-reward accumulated candidate.

E1.justification: V2 adds helpfulness/harmlessness response generation using HH-RLHF and a WMT24 Metrics Shared Task analysis covering en-de, en-es, and ja-zh. The literary translation directions and the zh-en/en-zh alignment sanity-check coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The established baseline families remain, but the translation comparison removes the SFT-plus-Plan2Align configuration from v1 Table 1. V2 also specifies final reward-based selection across accumulated candidates for Vanilla MPC. Best-of-10 and Best-of-20 are configurations of the existing Best-of-N comparator, rather than new baseline families.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a length-selected HH-RLHF protocol with 6,000 training and 1,024 test examples, response-quality metrics, GPT-4 judging, and an equal-generation Best-of-10 control. Reported settings also change: LoRA alpha 16 to 128, reward-model learning rate 1e-5 to 2e-5, DPO/SimPO learning rates 1e-6 to 5e-6, and translation buffer threshold 2 to 1. These disclosures do not establish that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: V1's translation iteration sweeps and Reference-versus-Annotation prompt ablation disappear (Tables 3, 6, and 7). V2 adds response-generation controls examining planning versus sampling/refinement, plus a systematic MetricX sentence-deletion analysis (Appendix H.1, Figure 9). The earlier alignment sanity check and three metric failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: V2 adds Kendall's tau estimation against document-level MQM targets, including constructed error penalties and normalization using each annotator's score distribution (Appendix H.1). The existing sanity-check means and standard deviations remain unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds HH-RLHF outcomes, including Plan2Align reward 4.5953 and GPT-4 win/loss rates of 46.8%/12.2% against DPO (Figure 3). Translation results are replaced: Plan2Align zh-en CW-COMET changes from 94.13 to 94.62 and d-BLEU from 21.17 to 15.76; zh-de CW-COMET changes from 92.60 to 91.73. Vanilla MPC values also change, while translation timing and ablation results disappear. These mixed updates accompany reported setting changes and are not established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The trajectory objective, Markov setup, and MPC optimization in Equations 1–2 remain. V2 adds an MPPI formulation with exponentially weighted control aggregation and a temperature parameter (Equation 3). This expands the mathematical background without adding theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the contribution from paragraph-level translation to LLM preference alignment encompassing long-form assistant responses. V2 foregrounds inference efficiency and cross-task applicability. V1's demonstrated augmentation of an SFT model is no longer presented as an established contribution.

C2.justification: V1's explanations of iteration degradation through semantic overload and language-dependent final-prompt effectiveness are removed with their analyses. V2 adds interpretations of the equal-generation response comparisons and explicitly limits Plan2Align to behaviors supported by the base model's output distribution. This replaces the earlier emphasis on language-coverage limitations with a broader capability boundary.

D1.justification: V2 adds response-generation and GPT-4 evaluation prompts, expanded pseudocode, Vanilla MPC prompting details, and the GPT-4 tokenizer disclosure. Training and buffer hyperparameters are revised, while v1's SpaCy/VecAlign implementation recipe is omitted. Hardware and the promised MIT release remain. Reproducibility is limited by differing HH-RLHF filtering descriptions and inconsistent segmentation descriptions: response thirds versus three-sentence segments.

R1.justification: V1's document-level translation positioning is replaced by separate discussions of fine-tuning and test-time preference alignment. V2 expands criticism of value-guided decoding and its overhead, adds RE-Control and MPPI positioning, and cites SimCSE and the WMT24 metrics study. Several translation-context works disappear; this substantially changes research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around general preference alignment. Context terminology becomes segment/reference-buffer terminology, experiments are reorganized by task, and limitations, impacts, evaluation details, and full translation results are redistributed across expanded appendices.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two-column to single-column layout and redraws Figures 1–2 around general control and segment selection. It adds the HH-RLHF results/win-rate display and six-panel MetricX plot. The main translation table is condensed with full metrics retained in Appendix D, while timing and ablation tables are removed.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the empirical case with GPT-4 comparisons on 1,024 HH-RLHF prompts and an equal-generation Best-of-10 control, providing corroboration beyond the inference reward and a clearer test of planning versus sampling. The additional MetricX analysis also supports evaluation choices. These gains are tempered by removed iteration/prompt ablations, lost alignment implementation details, and unclear HH-RLHF filtering and segmentation descriptions, making the net improvement limited.
